checked_sources: independent_checks.py: Prüfer enumeration, canonical forms, and recursive Littlestone game
correctness.rationale: For n>=3, centers have distinct closed neighborhoods: duplicate adjacent centers would have unequal connections to a third vertex in a tree. Any query v divides centers into N[v] and B_v=V\N[v]. The positive branch has Ldim<=2 because every second query retains at most two centers on one side (neighbors in a tree have no triangles); it has Ldim exactly two iff degree(v)>=3. The negative branch has Ldim>=2 iff a query w splits B_v into two sets of size >=2, exactly 2<=|N[w] intersect B_v|<=|B_v|-2. A depth-four tree is excluded since its positive branch can never reach depth three. A depth-three root exists exactly when both positive and negative conditions hold. For n>=4 a leaf query has two positive and n-2 negative centers, so depth>=2; n=1,2 are singleton classes and n=3 has Ldim1. The eight-vertex witness degree>=3 and |B_v|>=4 are necessary, hence no seven-vertex witness. If three query vertices were shattered, the all-one center would force a missing exactly-two trace by the uniqueness of a path in a tree, so VC<=2. Independently reconstructed the full online-minimax recursion and canonical Prüfer-tree enumerator: all 23 unlabeled eight-vertex types matched, exactly 12 attained dimension three; all types of order<=7 matched the trichotomy.
residual_risks: The twelve-of-twenty-three numerical count is an exhaustive finite census conditional on verified Prüfer and canonical encodings, not an all-order graph count. Only undirected connected simple trees and radius one are covered.

value.rationale: Adaptive Littlestone depth, unlike static VC dimension, governs realizable online mistakes. The universal three-round cutoff on a natural graph concept class and the sharp eight-vertex first VC/Ldim separation identify a motivated structural boundary, not a routine numeric lookup.
residual_risks: No assertion for variable-radius balls, arbitrary graphs, or a complete forbidden-tree-minor characterization.

final_claim: For finite trees, radius-one closed-neighborhood concepts have Littlestone dimension at most three with a complete degree-and-intersection trichotomy, first three-level witness on eight vertices, 12 of 23 eight-vertex tree types, and VC dimension at most two.
limitations: Finite simple connected undirected trees, radius-one closed balls only.
Eight-vertex census finite and exhaustive; all-order bound is analytic.
